description: Two-person high school team from Denizli, Türkiye, passionate about space and technology. One of us handles coding and prototyping, with experience in embedded systems, drones and tech competitions; the other leads research and presentation. We're fast learners, hands-on, and excited to tackle a real NASA challenge. Our team is complete and we're not looking for new members.
summary: Space Relics is an app that you can explore the spacecrafts which is launched and never turned back to earth. To explore them, go wherever you want in the solar system freely! Discover 12 spacecrafts on the Moon, 12 on the Mars, 7 in the deep space. Learn all of the stories of the spacecrafts, take a look to the official photos, listen the offical records and learn crazy things.
details:
What does it do or how does it work: With the app, you can explore the spacecrafts that launched by NASA and never came back to the earth. To explore, you can move freely in the solar system, Mars, Moon and deep space. You can learn the stories, take a look to the real photos, real records and crazy things about the spacecrafts.

What benefits does it have: All spacecraft information is stored in a single CSV file, so anyone can add a new spacecraft without knowing how to code.

With the app, there's no more getting informations with boring texts. You must find the spacecraft first, than you can get the informations from NASA.

What is the intended impact of the project: The main goal is to prevent spacecrafts that have completed their missions from being forgotten.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project:
Coding language and the library: C++17, raylib 5.5 and CMake

Models: Blender and Krita for the sketchs

AI: Claude for the help

How is your project creative: We don't take the spacecrafts as a space thrash, we take them as a relic that have special stories.

There are only a few apps that you can move freely in the solar system.

We thought every age gap.

What factors did your team consider: We are using the real datas such as the locations, weights, dates, stories and more.

It's easy to use, easy to explore the spacecrafts. There's nothing complex.
